tests.procedure: Visual check in a clean transparent watch glass (protected from light). Hygroscopicity: weigh a vessel with stopper (m1), add about 2 g sample (m2), stand unstoppered in a climatic cabinet at 25 ± 1 °C for 24 h, stopper and weigh (m3); % increase in mass per the STM equation. Interpretation: very hygroscopic >= 15%, hygroscopic 2-15%, slightly hygroscopic < 2%.

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg of powdered sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same steps to classify; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL, then 1 mg in 10 mL, else practically insoluble. Protect from light.

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: IR identification: mix the substance intimately with potassium bromide and compress into a transparent pellet; compare the spectrum with that of Ubidecarenone RS.

tests.procedure: Melting point: determine on a sufficient amount of sample with a calibrated melting point apparatus.
Water content: determine on about 3.00 g with a calibrated Karl Fischer titrator.

Sulphated ash (BP Appendix IX A): crucible previously ignited at 600-650 °C, cooled (W0); weigh 1.0 g (W1 = crucible + material); moisten with about 1 mL sulfuric acid, heat gently until charred, moisten again, heat until white fumes cease; ignite in muffle at 600-650 °C to constant weight (W2). % = (W2 - W0) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
